project.name: mac-control
project.identity: macctl, a command-first owner-only macOS control plane with a guarded local daemon, socket, and explicit Apple permission boundaries.
project.audience: The owner and local automation that need inspectable, permission-aware control of supported macOS capabilities.
project.core_loop: Discover a supported capability, request it through the guarded local control plane, inspect permission and execution evidence, and recover or stop when the boundary is not satisfied.
project.north_star: Local macOS control is explicit, owner-scoped, inspectable, and recoverable rather than hidden behind unsafe automation.
not_this: A permission bypass or stealth automation tool
A daemon that treats unverified effects as success

mvp.definition: The owner can discover and invoke supported local capabilities through macctl with explicit permission checks and machine-readable outcomes.

complete_product.definition: The control plane safely covers its supported macOS capability set with stable command, daemon, socket, permission, audit, and recovery behavior.

outcomes.name: A local capability invocation is bounded by owner scope, explicit permissions, and an inspectable result.

layers.intended: The owner retains control over which macOS effects are requested and trusted.
layers.planned: The project defines macctl, a daemon, local socket, and Apple framework boundaries.
layers.implemented: The repository contains the command-first control-plane implementation.
layers.verified: Repository documentation establishes the security boundary; no fresh TCC or daemon invocation was run here.

evidence.note: Defines macctl, owner-only scope, daemon, socket, and permission boundary.
Provides repository context and local ownership constraints.

blockers.summary: macOS TCC permissions and live daemon/device behavior require owner-controlled verification.

outcomes.name: A command result distinguishes permitted, denied, unavailable, attempted, and verified local effects.

layers.intended: The control plane never turns a request into an unsupported success claim.
layers.planned: The command-first surface and local socket are intended to make outcomes inspectable.
layers.implemented: The repository contains the control-plane surfaces and documented permission handling.
layers.verified: No live permission matrix or effect verification was performed in this bootstrap.

blockers.summary: Capability-by-capability positive, negative, and ambiguous trigger evidence remains incomplete.

verified.note: Documented claims only; no live permission or effect run here.

drift.summary: The owner-scoped control outcome depends on live macOS permission and effect evidence that documentation alone cannot establish.

evidence.note: Documents the control boundary without live TCC proof.
